scientific_queries.note: Self-diagnostic of the R72/R73 pool definition and tie-breaking.

subagent_note: None dispatched: the round audits its own two previous rounds, finds a mislabelled pool and an overly strict pre-registered threshold.

label_error.what_the_pool_actually_is: unseen cell AND at least one unseen drug
label_error.cause: the code's drug_seen requires BOTH drugs seen, so its negation means at least one is unseen

tiebreak_check.disclosure: the 0.5 pp threshold was arbitrary and noise-sized; I replaced it with a paired test and record that replacement here

decisions.H187_note: true under the paired test, false under the over-strict pre-registered threshold; both recorded

consequence_for_R72_R73.direction_unchanged: the annotation ridge still loses to the marginal baseline
consequence_for_R72_R73.reading_narrowed: because 90% of that pool retains one seen drug, the marginal baseline is NOT information-free there; the correct claim is 'the model loses wherever the baseline has partial information, and where the baseline has none (R66's both-unseen pool) it beats random only marginally at +1.25 pp with a CI lower bound of 0.00'

corrections_made: a new claim C48 records the mislabelling and the tie-break test
R72 and R73 documents left unmodified per the no-rewrite rule; this round is the correction of record
methodological_lesson: a pre-registered threshold that is the same size as the noise must be re-tested statistically afterwards, and the substitution must be recorded rather than silently applied
limits: only this one pool was diagnosed; other rounds' pools are not yet re-checked
the paired test uses 40 evaluation splits, so the CI is wide (about +/-0.8 pp)
the pre-registered criterion was replaced after seeing the data, which weakens rather than strengthens the claim
retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI
next_gates: re-check the pool labels in R66 (both_unseen) and R68 (strict) to establish whether 'both drugs unseen' was ever actually tested
